subject: chemistry
title: Structural formulae, isomers and naming
key_idea: A structural formula shows how the atoms in a molecule are arranged. Organic compounds are named from the number of carbons and the functional group. Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.

sections.heading: Ways to write an organic molecule

blocks.text: One molecule can be written in several ways. This section covers the types of formula and the words used for families of compounds.

items.meaning: The number of atoms of each element in one molecule, e.g. C₂H₆O.
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element.
One formula that fits every member of a homologous series, e.g. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes.
An unambiguous description of how the atoms are arranged, e.g. CH₃CH₂OH.
Shows every atom and every bond as a drawing.
A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula.
The atom or group of atoms that decides the chemical reactions of a compound.

items: Ethane has the molecular formula C₂H₆ and the empirical formula CH₃.
Ethanol has the molecular formula C₂H₆O and the structural formula CH₃CH₂OH.
Ethene is written CH₂=CH₂. The double bond is part of the structural formula.
Methyl ethanoate is written CH₃COOCH₃. It shows the order of the atoms, so it cannot mean anything else.
Members of a series have similar chemical properties. Each differs from the next by one CH₂ group, and they show a trend in physical properties, such as boiling point.
In a displayed formula, carbon forms four bonds, oxygen two and hydrogen one. A C=O or C=C is drawn as a double bond.
A structural formula shows the arrangement of atoms. A molecular formula only shows the numbers.
A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond.
A homologous series shares a functional group and a general formula.

blocks.text: The name has a stem for the length of the carbon chain and an ending for the functional group.

items: The first five alkanes are methane CH₄, ethane CH₃CH₃, propane CH₃CH₂CH₃, butane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and pentane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
The first three alkenes are ethene CH₂=CH₂, propene CH₂=CHCH₃ and butene.
Butene has two unbranched forms. **But-1-ene** is CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ and **but-2-ene** is CH₃CH=CHCH₃.
The number gives the first carbon of the double bond, counting from the end that gives the lower number.
Propanol has two forms. **Propan-1-ol** is CH₃CH₂CH₂OH and **propan-2-ol** is CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.
Butanol also has two unbranched forms. **Butan-1-ol** is CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH and **butan-2-ol** is CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃.
The number gives the carbon that carries the –OH group.

blocks.text: The carbon of the –COOH group counts in the chain, so ethanoic acid has two carbons.

items: The stem gives the number of carbons: meth, eth, prop, but, pent, hex.
The ending gives the series: -ane, -ene, -ol, -oic acid.
A number shows where the C=C or –OH is on the chain.

blocks.text: An ester is made from an alcohol and a carboxylic acid. Its name comes from both parent compounds.

items: The ester group is –COO–.
The first word comes from the alcohol and ends in **-yl**: methanol gives methyl, ethanol gives ethyl.
The second word comes from the acid and ends in **-oate**: ethanoic acid gives ethanoate, butanoic acid gives butanoate.

items.text: Butanoic acid and ethanol make ethyl butanoate.
The acid chain comes first and joins through COO to the alcohol chain: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₃.
In CH₃COOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ the chain after COO has four carbons (butyl) and the acid part has two (ethanoate): butyl ethanoate.

items: Methyl ethanoate is CH₃COOCH₃.
Ethyl ethanoate is CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.
Propyl butanoate has 7 carbon atoms in total: 4 from butanoic acid and 3 from propan-1-ol.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Structural formulae are sorted into alkanes, alkenes and alcohols.
diagram.prompt: Sort each structural formula into the right homologous series.

items: An ester name has the alcohol part first (-yl) and the acid part second (-oate).
Count the carbons on each side of COO to work out the parent alcohol and acid.

blocks.text: Some molecular formulae can be written as more than one structural formula. This section covers what that means and the examples you need.

items.meaning: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.

items: Pentane, C₅H₁₂, has three isomers. Only one of them is unbranched.
Isomers can be in the same series, such as butane and methylpropane.
Isomers can also be in different series, such as an ester and a carboxylic acid with the same formula.
To spot isomers, count each atom to check the molecular formula, then compare how the atoms are joined.
Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
Different arrangements can give different names and different properties.

checks.q: State what is meant by the term structural isomers.
checks.a: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.

checks.q: Name the ester made from propanoic acid and methanol, and write its structural formula.
Write the structural formulae of propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.
checks.a: Propan-1-ol is CH₃CH₂CH₂OH. Propan-2-ol is CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.

worked_example.question:
Hydrogen is the first element of the Periodic Table. For each of the homologous series shown, name a member that contains six hydrogen atoms.
● alkanes
● alkenes
● alcohols
● carboxylic acids
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct name. Check the hydrogen count in the formula, including the hydrogen in –OH and –COOH.

items: Know that a structural formula is an unambiguous description of how the atoms are arranged.
Write structural isomers of C₄H₁₀ and C₄H₈, as in the table.
Name and draw alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids (up to four carbons) and the unbranched esters made from them.

worked_example.question: This question is about hydrocarbons. The molecular formula C₄H₈ represents all the isomers of an alkene. Explain what is meant by the term isomers.
answer_points: Compounds with the same molecular formula.
But different structural or displayed formulae (different arrangements of atoms).
worked_example.tip: The second mark does not depend on the first, so give both points.
